clue.text: Moment back

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a very brief instant of time
to support a motion or a person formally

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words suggest an instant spent looking backwards; they are two unrelated meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a tiny unit of time and also a verb meaning to endorse or support a proposal.

clue.text: Tidy tree aloft

parts.note: a spruce is a type of conifer
aloft means up high

explanation.surface: Someone trims a tree high up in its branches.
explanation.definitionFit: To smarten or neaten something is a common phrasal-verb synonym for making it orderly.

clue.text: Bill's partner has carried peer around a US state

indicators.note: something carried is held inside, so the first piece wraps round what follows

parts.note: lovers are said to bill and coo

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the peer encloses the next little word

parts.note: a lord is a peer of the realm
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man’s companion has escorted a nobleman on a tour of an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill and coo' is the idiom for lovers whispering sweet nothings; Bill looks like a man's name but is the beak-touching verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado is one of the fifty states of America, in the Rocky Mountain region.

clue.text: Feature one runs occasionally

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a part of the face
second meaning: something that drips when you have a cold

explanation.walkthrough: The second half sounds like an athlete who jogs now and then; it is the facial part that streams during a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: The nose is a facial feature, and a nose is said to run when mucus drips during illness.

clue.text: Ooze inside pipe clearing

indicators.note: inside places the first word's letters within the word that follows

parts.note: to pipe is to sing in a high voice
a wound that weeps oozes fluid

explanation.surface: Sludge is seeping inside a drainpipe that is being unblocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipe' looks like a tube for plumbing, but here it is the verb meaning to sing shrilly.
explanation.definitionFit: Brushing a floor or chimney with a broom removes dirt, so the act is a form of tidying away.

clue.text: Pub with ale gone unfortunately, last of bitter drunk

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are knocked out of order
drunk means staggering and disordered, so the letters reel into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: last of asks for the final letter only of the following word

parts.note: the final letter of bitter

explanation.surface: A bar has run out of beer, sadly, and the last of the bitter has been drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British style of pale, hoppy beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Watering hole is informal slang for a bar where people gather to drink, from animals gathering at water.

clue.text: Flier tucked inside newspaper, neglected

indicators.note: tucked inside says the letters sit within the run of words that follows

parts.note: the end of newspaper and the start of neglected

explanation.surface: A leaflet has been slipped inside a newspaper and ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' looks like a printed leaflet, but here it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a bird and therefore something that flies.

clue.text: Country's literary king's one up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic monarch
the possessive ending supplies its letter
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A nation boasts that a famous fictional monarch's single act is going up.
explanation.walkthrough: LEAR'S I written upwards spells ISRAEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a sovereign nation in the Middle East on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Two articles supporting chap in South American country

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting places these pieces underneath the one they hold up

parts.note: guy is an informal word for a man
the indefinite articles an and a

explanation.surface: A pair of newspaper pieces back a man living in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Guyana is a nation on the northern coast of the South American continent, formerly British Guiana.

clue.text: Take great pleasure in dip

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to enjoy something keenly
second meaning: a savoury sauce or chutney

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like enjoying a swim; dip is the noun for a tangy condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning to savour with delight and a noun for a piquant sauce or pickle.

clue.text: Fish isn't swimming, ashen in Florida?

indicators.note: swimming suggests moving about freely, so these letters drift into a new order

parts.note: the letters of the contraction, apostrophe dropped
ashen means grey, spelt the American way as in Florida

explanation.surface: A fish lies still off Florida, looking pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Florida' asks for the American spelling: gray, not grey.
explanation.definitionFit: The stingray is a flat cartilaginous sea creature with a venomous barbed tail, so a kind of fish.

clue.text: Place above hand for last stretch

indicators.note: in a down entry, above means the first piece is written over the second

parts.note: one's home is one's place
a straight is a poker hand of five cards in sequence

explanation.surface: Positioning something over your hand ready for one final reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' suggests the body part, but it is a holding in poker.
explanation.definitionFit: The final level section of a racetrack before the finishing post is the closing part of a race.

clue.text: Jack, say: knave about right!

definitions.note: an example: the jack is one playing card

indicators.note: about means going round, so the knave wraps the next letter

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a rogue
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone declares that a man named Jack is a rotter, and right about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Knave is also the old name for the jack in a pack of cards, which makes the surface feel all about cards, but here it means a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The jack is one example of a playing piece from a standard pack.

clue.text: Directors twiddling thumbs, reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so we want a word pronounced like the phrase's meaning

parts.note: someone twiddling their thumbs is idle and fed up

explanation.surface: Company executives sit idle with nothing to do, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's governing group of executives is collectively called its board.

clue.text: Gas one converted, nitrogen

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: One kind of gas is turned into nitrogen.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is a noble chemical element that exists as a colourless inert vapour used in glowing signs.

clue.text: After uprising, country has embraced southern religion

indicators.note: in a down entry an uprising turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards
embracing means holding inside, so the country wraps the next letter

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: Following a revolt, a nation has adopted a faith from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: MALI written upwards is ILAM, and S goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is the monotheistic faith founded by the prophet Muhammad, followed by Muslims.

clue.text: Attack with stone, roughly

indicators.note: roughly means approximately or carelessly, so the letters are given in a loose order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An assault carried out by hurling a rock crudely.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset can mean an assault or charge, as in the onset of an enemy force.

clue.text: Lacking good judgment, mad using dinner to welcome leader of Conservatives

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them in, so the scrambled letters hold the next piece
mad means crazed and disordered, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: leader of asks for the first letter only of the following word

parts.note: the first letter of Conservatives

explanation.surface: It is foolish, even crazy, to use a dinner to win over the Tory leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled letters become UNDIS-ERNING, with C placed in the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without discernment cannot tell good from bad, so they show poor taste or judgement.

clue.text: Enthralling work of engineer?

definitions.note: a noun phrase: the activity of fastening with metal pins
definitions.meaning: second meaning: hammering metal pins to join plates

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal sense: hammering metal fasteners is what a riveter or engineer does.
explanation.definitionFit: A gripping story holds attention fixed, and the noun names fixing steel plates with headed bolts.

clue.text: African eating crusts on pasty, remarkably

indicators.note: remarkably suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters are made into an unusual arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: crusts are the outer edges, so only the outside letters of the next word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of pasty

explanation.surface: A person from Africa munches the pastry edges of a pie, notably.
explanation.walkthrough: A pasty is a pastry turnover with a savoury filling; 'eating' is fodder, not a containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Egypt is a person from a nation in the north-east of the continent.

clue.text: Painting, say, expression of enjoyment in hold, performing acrobatics

indicators.note: in places the first two pieces within the word that follows

parts.note: to cling is to grip tightly
painting is an example of art
whee is a cry of delight

explanation.surface: Someone shrieking with joy while hanging on, mid-gymnastics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold' looks like a grip in wrestling or gymnastics, but it is a verb whose letters enclose the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning sideways handsprings, hands then feet over and over, is a classic gymnastic stunt.

clue.text: Help-yourself food, big hit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a self-service spread of dishes
second meaning: a heavy blow or battering

explanation.walkthrough: 'Big hit' suggests a popular success; here it is a buffeting blow, a different pronunciation of the same spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffet is a meal laid out for guests to serve themselves, and a buffet is also a hard knock.

clue.text: Loud weapon standard, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: by the sound of it means as it is heard, so a word pronounced the same is wanted

parts.note: a canon is a standard or rule by which things are judged

explanation.surface: A noisy gun is regulation issue, or so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A large mounted gun firing heavy shot makes a booming report, hence a noisy piece of artillery.

clue.text: US state without a hope's captured

indicators.note: captured means held inside, so the letters lie within the words before

parts.note: the end of without, the word a, and the start of hope

explanation.surface: An American state with no chance has been seized.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty states of America, in the western mountain region.

clue.text: Heartless line ending great story

indicators.note: ending means coming at the close, so this piece follows the next one

parts.note: fab is short for fabulous, meaning great

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle, so only the outside letters of the next word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of line

explanation.surface: A cruel closing line makes a great tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A fable is a short tale, often with animals as characters, that teaches a moral lesson.

clue.text: Record by that man, old song

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: he is the pronoun for that man
an LP is a long-playing vinyl record

explanation.surface: A disc made by a certain man contains a golden oldie.
explanation.walkthrough: Help! is a 1965 Beatles hit, so an old song.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles released Help! in 1965, title track of their album and film, now a decades-old pop classic.

clue.text: Uplifting stuff, brandy

indicators.note: in a down entry, uplifting raises the word so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: to stuff is to cram

explanation.surface: Inspiring material, this spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is a French spirit distilled from the skins and pips left after pressing grapes for wine.

clue.text: Those eventually attacked, lowering heads, duck

indicators.note: heads are the tops, so the first letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the initial letters of those four words

explanation.surface: Those assaulted at last lowered their heads and ducked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like a verb for dodging blows, but it is the bird; 'lowering' is one of the words whose first letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a small freshwater dabbling waterfowl species of the dabbling kind.

clue.text: Cooler hugs with energy in dance

indicators.note: hugging holds something close inside, so the first word wraps the next

parts.note: a fan cools the air
and means together with
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A calmer person embraces someone energetically on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' suggests a calmer person, but it is the device that moves air.
explanation.definitionFit: The fandango is a lively Spanish courtship step in triple time, danced with castanets.

clue.text: Sign Mussolini, megalomaniac, somewhat taken aback

indicators.note: taken aback suggests going backwards, so the run of letters is read right to left
somewhat means only a part, so the letters are a portion of the words that follow

parts.note: the end of Mussolini and the start of megalomaniac

explanation.surface: The Italian dictator, power-mad, is a little startled by an omen.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the twins, is one of the twelve astrological star signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Resolution X passed by a municipality

indicators.note: passed by means placed alongside, so the later pieces follow the first

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
taken as written
a city is a municipality

explanation.surface: A council passes a numbered motion, Resolution X.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolution' looks like a formal council motion, which 'passed' supports; it means determination.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenacity and resolution both mean firm determination, a dogged refusal to give up.

clue.text: Hard work, an advertising phrase

parts.note: a slog is a long, hard task
taken as written

explanation.surface: Writing ad copy is a real grind.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchy motto used in marketing to promote a brand or product is a typical tagline.
